translation_direction: da → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Danish electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Vietnamese capitalisation is used after an internal ! where a new clause begins, although the Danish witness continues in lower case.
decisions.rationale: Lower case after ! reads as an error in Vietnamese; the exclamations themselves are preserved.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Andersen’s recurring gamle Mormor had been flattened to bà three times; now bà ngoại già / bà ngoại throughout, with Bà ơi! kept for the cry.
The bystanders’ Hun har villet varme sig is flat and inferential: Chắc nó định sưởi cho ấm, người ta bảo — without an added exclamation.
næsten ganske døde af Kulde keeps død (gần như đã chết vì rét), anticipating 1.9; the parallel hvor sprudede den, hvor brændte den restored.
The mother had worn the slippers most recently, not ‘for the last time’; the boy’s selv restored.
Nu dør der en is present: Có ai đang chết đấy!
Glans rendered as hào quang throughout; velsignet as warmth rather than religious blessing; bà ẵm cô bé; hai bà cháu đã ở bên Chúa.
forkuet as cowed (rụt rè, khổ sở).
Capitalisation after internal ! normalised to Vietnamese convention; Tromle as thân lò.

Second-pass fixes: they lived just under the roof (garret), hands tê dại rather than ‘dead’, varied the repeated sưởi ấm, aligned velsignet in 1.3 and 1.8, holde paa as keeping her there, thi thể for Lig, de mange Julelys as muôn vàn.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Several Vietnamese translations under the title Cô bé bán diêm are widely known; their sources, completeness and reuse status were not audited here. No absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: bà ngoại già / bà ngoại; Bà ơi! in address
glossary.rationale: Andersen repeats the formula; Mormor is specifically the maternal grandmother.
Distinguishes the radiance of the final vision from ordinary light (Lys).
Ordinary Vietnamese word; the title follows the established Cô bé bán diêm.

witness_decision: Selected the tale as printed in H. C. Andersen, Eventyr, vol. 2 (København: Det Nordiske Forlag, E. Bojesen, 1900), printed pp. 169–173, from the Internet Archive scan eventyr02ande (Getty Research Institute copy). This posthumous edition uses post-1892 Danish spelling. The unsourced Danish Wikisource text in older spelling was not used because its witness is undocumented. First published in Dansk Folkekalender for 1846 (December 1845); not collated.

unresolved_questions.explanation: Cô bé bán diêm is the established Vietnamese title; the Danish literally says ‘the little girl with the matches’, and bán (selling) is supplied from the story.

title_review.rationale: Cô bé bán diêm is the title by which Vietnamese readers know the tale. It is not literal (the Danish names ‘the little girl with the matches’), but the story shows her selling matches, and the established title avoids presenting a familiar work under an unrecognisable name.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Compared the cold evening, the slippers, the matches, the corner, home and the first match with the stove.
Compared the goose, the Christmas tree, the falling star and the grandmother’s saying.
Compared the grandmother’s appearance, the last matches, the ascent and the morning discovery.
